references.text: The verse describes that the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas Iscariot to betray Jesus, confirming his role as a traitor.
Jesus points directly to Judas Iscariot as the one he gives bread to, and confirms that it is him who will betray him.
Mark reports that Judas Iscariot went to the chief priests to betray Jesus, and they were glad about this.
Luke tells us that Satan entered Judas Iscariot, who was one of the twelve, and he went to the chief priests to betray Jesus.
Matthew describes how Judas Iscariot went to the chief priests and offered to betray Jesus for money.
